title: Loadgen orchestration: sweep matrix and observability notes
content:
Purpose
This is a working note describing an orchestration-first approach to throughput benchmarking for the serving runtime. The aim is to (1) codify a sweep matrix that covers realistic axes of variability, (2) define orchestration primitives (epochs and checkpoints) so runs are repeatable and resumable, and (3) enumerate observability hooks and artifact capture that make debugging and postmortem analysis straightforward.

Why this is different
Many of our prior docs focus on warmup recipes and load patterns. This note prioritizes orchestration: how to combine many micro-parameters into structured experiments and how to record the minimum set of telemetry to guarantee deterministic reproduction within +/- small noise bands. Emphasis on resumability (long-running sweep jobs), artifact naming, and automated sanity assertions.

High-level design
- Unit of work: experiment epoch. An epoch is a single stable configuration run intended to produce a steady-state throughput and latency distribution for N minutes. Epochs are the building blocks of larger sweeps.
- Sweep: an ordered list of epochs that iterates across a defined parameter matrix (see sweep matrix section). Sweeps are checkpointed after each epoch so long running jobs can resume if interrupted.
- Runner: the orchestration controller that schedules epochs against one or more target clusters, tracks artifacts, and verifies post-epoch assertions.

Sweep matrix (recommended minimal axes)
Each sweep should be constructed from combinations of the axes below. Start small (2–3 levels per axis) and expand. Record the matrix in a CSV artifact for traceability.
- model_variant: [gpt-small-q4f, gpt-medium-fp16, gpt-medium-qat]
- concurrency_profile: [single-client, 8-cohort, poisson-200rps] (maps to client concurrency and arrival pattern)
- occupancy (per-GPU): [0.25, 0.5, 0.9] (fraction of slot occupancy expected under target throughput)
- sequence_length_distribution: [short(8), mixed(mean=128), long(512)] (attach input corpus id)
- batch_policy: [auto-batch, fixed-32, disabled]
- kv_cache_mode: [disabled, per-session, global-shared]
- request_size_bytes: [small, medium, large] (for embedding or non-text payloads)
- quant_mode: [fp16, int8, q4f]
- region_routing: [local, cross-region-fallback]

Experiment orchestration primitives
- epoch_id: UUID assigned to each epoch. Used in artifact naming.
- seed: global RNG seed (string) used to derive traffic order, payload selection, and simulated user ids. Store seed with epoch metadata.
- epoch_duration: nominal steady-state duration in minutes (recommended 10–30). Shorter durations for micro-sanity checks, longer for stability sweeps.
- warmup_phase: pre-epoch short run that establishes kernel caches and model paths. Warmup is checkpointed separately.
- checkpoints: after warmup and after each epoch. Checkpoint artifact includes: runner logs, client logs, target node perf counters, flamegraphs, and a small snapshot of token-level timing for 1% of requests.
- resume_policy: how to continue after interruption. Options: retry_epoch_from_start, resume_epoch_from_checkpoint, skip_epoch. Default: resume_epoch_from_checkpoint when checkpoint exists and is verified.

Traffic generation and determinism
- Deterministic corpus selection: Use the seed to select an ordered list of inputs. Inputs should be kept in immutable, versioned corpora (S3 path with hash).
- Arrival patterns: Support deterministic Poisson replay (derived from seed) and fixed inter-arrival sequences. For noisy arrival (jittered-poisson) capture the RNG outputs to reproduce exact event times.
- Client-side batching simulation: If we emulate multiple clients, each virtual client runs a deterministic schedule seeded by (seed + client_index).
- RNG hygiene: All sources of randomness (payload permutation, tokenization threading, arrival jitter) must expose seed and RNG type in epoch metadata.

Warmup and priming (checkpoint-based)
- Two-phase: quick kernel priming (30–60s) followed by session priming for caches (3–5 min) for long-sequence or kv-heavy workloads.
- Checkpoint after kernel priming: record GPU kernel selection table and shared library versions. If kernels differ between priming and epoch, flag run as invalid.
- Priming validation: measure key indicators (KV hit rate, L2 cache warm ratio, first-token latencies) and assert they fall within expected bands before promoting to full epoch.

Observability and artifacts (what to capture)
Capture the following and bundle them with the epoch artifact store (object path includes epoch_id and seed):
- Runner metadata JSON (epoch_id, seed, config matrix row, git commit of runner and serving-runtime)
- Client logs (structured JSONL) with request_id, timestamps (client send, server accept, server start generation, token emit times, completion), and request/response sizes
- Server traces: per-request span with route/model/variant tags; sampled at 100% during debugging sweeps, 1% for large sweeps
- GPU/perf counters: per-GPU utilization, SM occupancy, memory bandwidth, tensor core usage sampled at 1s resolution
- Kernel table and cuBLAS/cuDNN versions, libcudnn heuristics chosen
- Flamegraphs and CPU profiles from model process (top 5 threads)
- KV cache stats: hit/miss counters, occupancy over time
- System metrics: OS-level telemetry (iostat, vmstat, top) and Docker/K8s resource metrics
- A short deterministic trace subset (1% of requests) with token-level timing for reproducing tail latency issues

Automated assertions (post-epoch)
Each epoch should run post-checks before being marked successful:
- steady_state_check: coefficient of variation for throughput in last half of epoch < 0.04 (configurable)
- latency_stability: 95th percentile across last half of epoch within X% of median run for same config (X set per experiment group)
- priming_consistency: kernel table matches warmup checkpoint
- artifact_integrity: all expected artifacts uploaded and checksums verified
- seed_replay: optional quick replay of 1% of captured events to confirm deterministic matching
If any assertion fails, epoch is marked failed and runner emits a diagnostic bundle.

Noise mitigation strategies
- single-datapath isolation: dedicate nodes for runs (no co-tenants) when measuring micro-optimizations
- controlled background noise: if we need to test under realistic multi-tenant noise, include a separate sweep axis for background load generator and tag artifacts accordingly
- replicate epochs: run each epoch at least 3 times in separate allocations to estimate experimental noise and compute confidence intervals

Result aggregation and metadata model
- Canonical result: a single line CSV per epoch with columns: epoch_id, seed, model_variant, occupancy, concurrency_profile, batch_policy, seq_dist, throughput_mean, throughput_p95, latency_p50, latency_p95, gpu_util_mean, kv_hit_rate, artifact_path, run_status
- Store a small JSON metadata per sweep describing the full matrix, runner version, start/end times, and aggregate deviation statistics across replicates

Failure modes and debug playbook (quick)
- Non-repeatable spike in tail latency: Check client RNG logs for arrival burst, check kernel table drift, confirm no background cron jobs on nodes.
- Throughput plateau below expected: Verify batch_policy engaged (server-side batching logs), check KV cache misses and memory thrashing, compare kernel table.
- Intermittent OOM/GC: capture process heap profiles and GPU allocation timeline, correlate to request payload sizes.

Operationalizing the runner
- Provide a CLI: run-sweep --matrix <csv> --corpus <s3path> --resume --artifact-root <s3root> --parallelism 2
- Expose a lightweight web UI to inspect current sweep progress, view epoch artifacts, and trigger replays for individual epoch seeds
- Integrate with CI for fast-checks: on PRs touching serving runtime, run a tiny sweep (3 epochs) against a smoke cluster to ensure no regressions in kernel selection or basic throughput.

Quick checklist (pre-flight)
- [ ] corpora versioned and checked-in to object store
- [ ] matrix CSV created and validated
- [ ] seed deterministic generator configured
- [ ] artifact-root path reserved and permissions set
- [ ] monitoring alert channel configured for runner failures

Appendix: example epoch metadata (fields to store)
- epoch_id, seed, matrix_row_id, model_variant, runner_git_sha, serving_runtime_git_sha, node_image, kernel_table_hash, start_ts, end_ts, epoch_duration_seconds, client_config_id, artifact_path

Open questions / work items
- Define a canonical small-corpus for quick smoke-checks that covers tokenization edge-cases
- Decide default replicate count for each axis (2 vs 3) based on resource budget
- Add lightweight end-to-end replay verification that runs inside a job in a sandboxed cluster to confirm seed replay correctness without exposing production nodes

Notes to reviewers
This is a draft. Looking for feedback on the axis list (are we missing an important one for production workloads?), sensible defaults for epoch_duration and replicate count, and whether checkpoint granularity is too heavy for continuous benchmarking.
